input.strategy_title: FIPS 140-3 compliance for the model serving stack
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Public-sector deals require the model serving stack to run on FIPS-enabled
OpenShift clusters using validated cryptographic modules. Today KServe
components and the serving data plane link non-validated crypto libraries in
several images, and we have no compliance evidence package. Certification
involves an external accredited laboratory (historical turnaround: six to nine
months) and mandatory security review board sign-off at defined milestones —
these human and third-party gates dominate the schedule regardless of
engineering speed.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | All serving-stack images run correctly on FIPS-enabled clusters using validated crypto modules (no non-validated crypto in the request path). |
| HLR-2 | P0 | A compliance evidence package (module inventory, build attestations, test results) is assembled and submitted through the security review board to the external certification lab. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | CI enforces FIPS regressions: a gating check fails any serving-stack build that reintroduces non-validated crypto usage. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation states the FIPS support posture and cluster prerequisites. |

## Affected Components

- KServe
- Platform Operator

## Out of Scope

- FIPS posture for workbenches, pipelines, and training (separate strategies)
- Common Criteria certification

## Open Questions

None on scope — but note that lab scheduling and review-board cadence are
externally controlled and cannot be compressed by engineering effort.

# FIPS 140-3 conversion of KServe serving-stack images

## Description

Converts the KServe serving-stack images so they run correctly on FIPS-enabled
OpenShift clusters using validated cryptographic modules, with no non-validated
crypto in the request path. The epic covers the audit of current cryptographic
library linkage, the conversion to validated modules, verification on a
FIPS-enabled cluster, and the CI regression enforcement covering KServe image
builds.

## Scope

- Audit all KServe serving-stack images to inventory every linked cryptographic
  library and its validation status; the audit determines the exact set of
  images needing conversion (the strategy says "several images" without
  enumerating them).
- Replace non-validated cryptographic library usage with validated modules
  throughout the request path.
- Rebuild the converted images and verify correct serving operation on a
  FIPS-enabled OpenShift cluster.
- Author and verify the CI gating check covering KServe image builds that
  fails any build reintroducing non-validated crypto usage — the KServe-surface
  portion of the FIPS regression enforcement, owned here because it enforces
  over exactly the images this epic converts.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A cryptographic module inventory exists for every KServe serving-stack image,
  listing each linked crypto library and its validation status.
- All KServe serving-stack images run correctly on a FIPS-enabled OpenShift
  cluster using validated crypto modules, with no non-validated crypto in the
  request path, verified by test.
- The CI gating check covering KServe image builds fails a build that
  reintroduces non-validated crypto usage, verified by a test that intentionally
  reintroduces such usage and observes the gate fail.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0) — KServe-image portion: images run on FIPS-enabled clusters with
  validated crypto, no non-validated crypto in the request path.
- HLR-3 (P1) — KServe-surface portion of the CI FIPS regression check
  (bundled: the check enforces over the same images this epic converts, so it
  is not separately schedulable).

## Risks / Notes

- The strategy does not enumerate which images link non-validated crypto; the
  scope audit resolves this and does not change the epic's shape.
- "Serving data plane" is interpreted as the KServe predictor data plane. If
  model-serving runtime images are also in scope, that work belongs to a
  separate strategy and epic set.

# FIPS 140-3 conversion of Platform Operator images

## Description

Converts the Platform Operator's images so the operator runs correctly on
FIPS-enabled OpenShift clusters using validated cryptographic modules. The epic
covers the audit of current cryptographic library linkage, the conversion to
validated modules, verification on a FIPS-enabled cluster, and the CI regression
enforcement covering Platform Operator image builds.

## Scope

- Audit all Platform Operator images to inventory every linked cryptographic
  library and its validation status; the audit determines the exact set of
  images needing conversion.
- Replace non-validated cryptographic library usage with validated modules.
- Rebuild the converted images and verify correct operator behavior
  (installation and reconciliation of the serving stack) on a FIPS-enabled
  OpenShift cluster.
- Author and verify the CI gating check covering Platform Operator image builds
  that fails any build reintroducing non-validated crypto usage — the
  operator-surface portion of the FIPS regression enforcement, owned here
  because it enforces over exactly the images this epic converts.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A cryptographic module inventory exists for every Platform Operator image,
  listing each linked crypto library and its validation status.
- The Platform Operator runs correctly on a FIPS-enabled OpenShift cluster
  using validated crypto modules, verified by test of installation and
  reconciliation of the serving stack.
- The CI gating check covering Platform Operator image builds fails a build
  that reintroduces non-validated crypto usage, verified by a test that
  intentionally reintroduces such usage and observes the gate fail.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0) — Platform Operator portion: operator images run on FIPS-enabled
  clusters with validated crypto.
- HLR-3 (P1) — operator-surface portion of the CI FIPS regression check
  (bundled: the check enforces over the same images this epic converts, so it
  is not separately schedulable).

## Risks / Notes

- No architecture-context file is provisioned for the Platform Operator, so its
  repo and image layout are unverified; confirm at implementation start. The
  component is treated as existing (it is in the canonical RHAI component list
  and the strategy presumes its images already ship).
- The owning team is inferred (the strategy has no team table) and should be
  confirmed by a human.

# FIPS 140-3 compliance evidence package and certification submission

## Description

Assembles the FIPS 140-3 compliance evidence package for the model serving
stack — cryptographic module inventory, build attestations, and test results —
and submits it through the security review board to the external accredited
certification laboratory.

## Scope

- Consolidate the cryptographic module inventory from the FIPS conversion
  audits of all serving-stack images in scope (KServe components and the
  Platform Operator).
- Collect the build attestations produced by the FIPS-converted serving-stack
  image builds.
- Collect the test results demonstrating correct operation on FIPS-enabled
  OpenShift clusters using validated crypto modules, with no non-validated
  crypto in the request path.
- Assemble the package in the form required by the security review board and
  the certification laboratory, drive it through the review-board milestones,
  and submit it to the laboratory.
- Track the submission through lab triage.

This epic runs in parallel with the image conversion work: the conversion
outputs (attestations, test results) are content the package includes, enforced
by the acceptance criteria below rather than by a scheduling dependency.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The evidence package includes the cryptographic module inventory covering
  every serving-stack image in scope.
- The evidence package includes the build attestations produced by the
  FIPS-converted serving-stack image builds.
- The evidence package includes the test results demonstrating correct
  operation on FIPS-enabled clusters using validated crypto modules with no
  non-validated crypto in the request path.
- The evidence package is assembled in the form required by the security
  review board and submitted through the security review board to the external
  certification laboratory.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0) — full: compliance evidence package (module inventory, build
  attestations, test results) assembled and submitted through the security
  review board to the external certification lab.

## Risks / Notes

- Laboratory turnaround is historically six to nine months and security review
  board sign-off occurs at defined milestones; both are externally controlled
  and cannot be compressed by engineering effort. This epic's deliverable ends
  at submission through the security review board — the certification outcome
  and its timing are outside the strategy's control. The submission is expected
  to be triaged/acknowledged by the laboratory after intake, but lab triage is
  an external party's action and is therefore tracked as an expectation here
  rather than an acceptance criterion.
- The package spans the whole serving stack (KServe components and the
  Platform Operator); the KServe component is recorded as the primary Jira
  component for routing.

# Documentation of the FIPS support posture and cluster prerequisites

## Description

Documents the FIPS support posture of the model serving stack and the cluster
prerequisites for running it on FIPS-enabled OpenShift clusters, produced
through the Red Hat docs content process.

## Scope

Content outline:

- FIPS support posture: which serving-stack components (KServe components and
  the Platform Operator) run with validated cryptographic modules on
  FIPS-enabled clusters.
- Cluster prerequisites for FIPS-enabled operation of the serving stack.
- The CI enforcement posture for FIPS regressions on serving-stack builds, and
  any known limitations.
- Publication through the Red Hat docs content process (authoring, technical
  review, publication).

## Acceptance Criteria

- The documentation states the FIPS support posture of the model serving stack
  and the cluster prerequisites for FIPS-enabled operation.
- The content is technically reviewed against the implemented FIPS conversion
  and evidence work for accuracy.
- The documentation is published through the Red Hat docs content process.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P2) — documentation states the FIPS support posture and cluster
  prerequisites.

## Risks / Notes

- The epic's priority (P0) derives from the strategy's Critical frontmatter
  priority via the docs-authoring priority exception, not from HLR-4's P2
  label.
- This epic starts only after all serving-stack implementation work is
  complete, so the documented posture reflects what was actually built.

# Decomposition Summary — RHAISTRAT-9013: FIPS 140-3 compliance for the model serving stack

Strategy status: Refinement Done. Strategy priority: Critical.

Triage: full decomposition. The strategy is not below-threshold — it affects two
components (KServe, Platform Operator), spans architecturally distinct work
streams (image code conversion, a compliance evidence process with external
submission, and documentation authoring), and is Critical priority. It is not
docs-only — HLR-1 requires code changes to serving-stack images.

## Epic List

| ID | Title | Type | Team | Priority |
|----|-------|------|------|----------|
| RHAISTRAT-9013-E001 | FIPS 140-3 conversion of KServe serving-stack images | Implementation | RHOAI Serving | P0 |
| RHAISTRAT-9013-E002 | FIPS 140-3 conversion of Platform Operator images | Implementation | RHOAI Platform | P0 |
| RHAISTRAT-9013-E003 | FIPS 140-3 compliance evidence package and certification submission | Implementation | RHOAI Serving | P0 |
| RHAISTRAT-9013-E004 | Documentation of the FIPS support posture and cluster prerequisites | Implementation (docs-authoring) | RHOAI Serving | P0 |

## Dependency DAG

```mermaid
graph TD
    E001["E001 KServe image FIPS conversion"] --> E004["E004 FIPS posture documentation"]
    E002["E002 Platform Operator image FIPS conversion"] --> E004
    E003["E003 Compliance evidence package and submission"] --> E004
```

E001, E002, and E003 are parallel roots; E004 is blocked by all three.

## DAG Justification

| Edge | Rule | Rationale |
|------|------|-----------|
| E001 → E004 | Rule 11 | docs-authoring epic is blocked by every Implementation epic — docs describe what was built. |
| E002 → E004 | Rule 11 | Same — docs-last rule. |
| E003 → E004 | Rule 11 | Same — docs-last rule. |
| no edge E001 ↔ E002 | Rules 1, 14 | Different components and repos, no shared build artifacts → parallel. |
| no edge E001/E002 ↔ E003 | Rule 13 (content-consumption clarification) | The evidence package consumes build attestations and test results as **content**, not as artifacts its code builds against. Rule 13 is explicit that build outputs consumed as content (attestations, scan results, test evidence) are AC gates on the consuming epic, never DAG edges. E003 therefore runs in parallel with the conversion work and is not complete until its inclusion ACs hold. |
| no edge for the external lab | Rule 21 / Step 5.5 | The accredited laboratory and security review board are third-party **process** gates, not engineering artifacts — no upstream PR/RFC exists to model as an epic. Modeled as tiered delivery (below) plus risk notes on E003. |
| no Investigation epics | Step 3 | The strategy states "None on scope" for open questions; no risks, assumptions, pending reviews, or conditional ADRs are recorded. Which specific images link non-validated crypto is unresolved, but the answer does not change which epics exist or what they do — it is the audit work inside each conversion epic (an acceptance criterion, per the Step 3 decision rule). |

## HLR Traceability Matrix

| HLR | Priority | Epic(s) |
|-----|----------|---------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | E001 (KServe images), E002 (Platform Operator images) — split by component per Epic Boundary Rule 1. |
| HLR-2 | P0 | E003 (full). |
| HLR-3 | P1 | E001 (bundled), E002 (bundled) — the CI FIPS regression check is a shared-surface enforcement deliverable: it enforces over exactly the images each conversion epic converts, so it is divided per surface (each conversion epic authors and verifies the check covering its own image builds) rather than carved into a standalone work-type epic. A standalone check epic would build the same enforcement surface twice and add an artificial serialization edge. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | E004 (docs-authoring). |

Full coverage: HLR-1 through HLR-4 are all mapped; no orphaned requirements.

Note on E004 priority: HLR-4 is P2, but docs-authoring epics take their priority
from the strategy frontmatter (`priority: Critical` → P0) per the docs-authoring
priority exception, and do not push priority upstream.

## Component and Team Mapping

- `KServe` and `Platform Operator` are both verbatim canonical component names from `.context/rhai-components.txt`.
- E003 (evidence package) spans both strategy components; assigned `KServe` as the single most-relevant canonical name because the compliance scope is the model serving stack, with the span noted here.
- E004 is assigned the canonical `Documentation` component.
- Teams: KServe ownership (RHOAI Serving) comes from `.context/architecture-context/architecture/rhoai-3.0/kserve.md`. The strategy has no Impacted Teams table; the Platform Operator team (RHOAI Platform) and the docs epic team are inferred — flagged in Health Warnings.

## Health Warnings

1. **Missing strategy sections** (non-blocking): the strategy has no Impacted Teams table, no Dependencies table, no Given/When/Then acceptance criteria, no NFRs, and no Staff Engineer Input. Decomposition proceeded from the HLR table, Affected Components list, and problem statement. Team assignments for E002 and E004 are inferred and should be verified by a human.
2. **No architecture-context file for Platform Operator**: the provisioned architecture-context snapshot contains only `rhoai-3.0/kserve.md`. Platform Operator is treated as an **existing** component — it is in the canonical RHAI component list and the strategy's premise is that its images already exist and link non-validated crypto (you cannot FIPS-convert images of a component that does not exist) — so no new-component onboarding chain (repo/license/konflux) was generated. The `architecture_claims` signal for E002 is scored 0 (no context file covers it). A human should confirm the operator's repo and image layout.
3. **Externally controlled schedule gates**: laboratory turnaround (historically six to nine months) and security review board cadence are outside engineering control. Per the AC rules these are recorded as Risks/Notes on E003, not as acceptance criteria; E003's ACs sit on the engineering completion point (package assembled and submitted through the security review board). The expectation that the laboratory triages/acknowledges the submission is likewise recorded in E003's Risks/Notes, since lab intake is an external party's action.
4. **Scope ambiguity — "serving data plane"**: the problem statement says "KServe components and the serving data plane" link non-validated crypto. Per the architecture context, model execution in the serving stack involves Serving Runtimes (vLLM, OpenVINO, Caikit). The Affected Components list names only KServe and Platform Operator, so the decomposition covers those two; if Serving Runtimes images are intended in scope, that is a strategy amendment requiring additional epics. Flagged for human confirmation.
5. **Priority note**: HLR-4 is P2 while its epic E004 carries P0 — this is the docs-authoring priority exception (strategy frontmatter Critical → P0), not an inversion. HLR-3 (P1) is bundled into the P0 conversion epics because its enforcement surface is identical to their conversion surface (recorded in the traceability matrix row above).

## Tiered Delivery

The external dependency with uncertain timing is the certification laboratory
(and the review board cadence). Partial value is deliverable without it, so the
strategy splits naturally:

- **Tier 1 (independent value)**: E001 and E002 — the serving stack runs
  correctly on FIPS-enabled OpenShift clusters using validated crypto modules,
  with CI regression enforcement (HLR-1, HLR-3). This is complete regardless of
  certification timing.
- **Tier 2 (externally gated)**: E003 — the evidence package is assembled and
  submitted (HLR-2); the certification *outcome* arrives on the lab's schedule
  after submission. E004 (HLR-4) follows all implementation work per the
  docs-last rule and documents the Tier 1 posture.

No DAG edge models the lab: it is a process gate on the certification outcome,
not a prerequisite for any engineering work (Rule 21 — third party resolves →
precondition with tiered delivery, no separate epic).

### 2. DAG Coherence (2/2)
